title: Directional Derivative: A Tilted Slice
topic: Directional derivative as the slope of a vertical slice. Pick a point on a surface z = f(x, y) and a unit direction u; the plane through that point parallel to u cuts the surface along a curve whose slope at the point is the directional derivative. Algebraically it equals the dot product of the gradient with u.

beats.narration: How fast does a hill climb if you walk it not east, not north, but at an angle? That's the directional derivative.

elements.content: Manimo bobs centre with caption 'A tilted slope.'

beats.narration: Here is a surface, z equals f of x comma y. At any point we already know two slopes — the partial derivatives — one along the x axis, one along the y axis.

elements.content: Contour plot of a bowl-shaped surface in chalk-300, mild paraboloid centred near origin
Axes in chalk-200 through the contour origin
x-axis partial-derivative arrow at point P, short, violet-400
y-axis partial-derivative arrow at point P, short, teal-400
Right panel: 'partial derivatives' eyebrow + f sub x + f sub y annotations on backdrop

beats.narration: Now pick any unit direction u. Walk a tiny step from the point in direction u. The slope of the surface along that step is the directional derivative.

elements.content: Faint partials remain in background, opacity 0.3
Unit vector u at point P, amber-400, longer arrow, labelled u
Dashed line through P along u — the slice trace on the contour plot
Right panel: 'a slice along u' eyebrow + 'the slope of the cut' caption on backdrop

beats.narration: The shortcut: take the gradient of f at the point, then dot it with u. The directional derivative of f in direction u equals the gradient of f dotted with u.

elements.content: Gradient arrow at P, perpendicular to contours, rose-400, labelled grad f
Unit vector u remains in amber-400
Small angle arc between grad f and u in chalk-200
Right panel: 'D u f = grad f dot u' eyebrow + big serif formula + footnote 'project the gradient onto the direction'

beats.narration: So every direction has its own slope, and the gradient is the one direction where that slope is largest.

elements.content: 'One gradient, every direction.' — serif italic 56px, 'every direction' in amber-300
'D u f equals grad f dot u — the slope along u.' — serif italic 26px
